thread:
maria: Heads up — saw sustained backpressure on the obs-ingest cluster around 07:40 UTC. Ingress queues ballooning for ~20m, tail latency spiking. Looks correlated with billing-tag enrichment spikes. Anyone else seeing this?

raj: Yep, saw the same. Enricher service doing lots of synchronous lookups to billing-store; when it slows everything piles up.

ana?? ana: Quick note: we have three knobs here: (1) apply backpressure at ingress (reject / throttle), (2) make enrichment async (post-ingest), (3) degrade enrichment (best-effort / partial tags). Tradeoffs below.

kevin: From SRE POV we prefer graceful degradation. Hard drop risks correctness but keeps latency bounded. Circuit-breaker around enrichers + automatic fallback to "tags_missing" marker.

liz: Concern: if we drop billing tags we lose cost attribution fidelity for those traces. Is there a cheap compromise?

raj: Proposed pattern: bounded, priority queue at ingest -> if queue full, spill to cold object storage (S3) for deferred enrichment. Also add a lightweight "cost_hint" flag on spans that marks high-value traces which should be enriched synchronously. Low-value spans go to deferred pipeline.

maria: That seems reasonable. Key Q: how do we decide "high-value"? sampler? token count? user tier?

raj: Start with simple heuristics: 1) traces with billing account present, 2) traces from dedicated customers (tenant tag), 3) traces above token threshold. We can refine with ML later.

sam: For realtime billing dashboards we need some traces enriched immediately. Can we mark routes that require synchronous enrich?

ana?? ana: Yes — add route-level config: `sync_enrich: true|false` in ingest config. Default false. Sync only for critical routes.

raj: Implementation sketch (pseudocode):

```
enqueue(span):
  if queue.size < BOUND:
    queue.push(span)
  else:
    if span.cost_hint or span.route.sync_enrich:
      apply_backpressure()  # reject / rate-limit upstream
    else:
      spill_to_s3(span)  # deferred pipeline
```

raj: We'll also emit metrics: `enricher.sync_rejects`, `enricher.spills`, `enricher.queue_depth`, and histogram of enrich latency. These drive alerts and autoscaling.

kevin: Add circuit-breaker metric `enricher.cb_open_seconds` so we can track how long we were in degraded mode. When CB open we should add a prominent log line and an incident page if >5min.

liz: What about billing accuracy SLA? Can we define an eventual consistency window (e.g., 1h) and track how many spans are enriched within window? Product can accept some delay if it's tracked.

maria: +1 to a defined SLA for deferred enrichment (e.g., 95% enriched within 1h). That lets us prioritize realtime work.

raj: Operational concerns: cold-spill backlog processing needs idempotency and ordering is not required for enrichment. Also need dedupe if same span retried. Add `ingest_id` and idempotent enrichment job.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: enrich-service v1.2.7 -> canary started at 07:25 UTC; 3/5 canaries healthy, 2 failed healthchecks -> rollback initiated.

kevin: That explains the timing. Canary failures plus slow billing-store produced the backpressure.

maria: Next steps: (a) quick patch to add `spill_to_s3` fallback + metrics (b) RFC for longer-term: priority queue + route-level `sync_enrich` + SLA for deferred enrichment (c) run a short chaos test to simulate billing-store slowness.

ana?? ana: I'll draft the RFC with diagrams and perf targets. Can we meet tomorrow 10:00 UTC for a 30m sync?

liz: Works for PMs.

raj: I'll prototype the spiller and metric hooks today.

kevin: I'll add the CB alert and a runbook entry for degraded enrichers.

sam: :thumbsup:

maria: Thanks all — filing follow-up RFC + calendar invite.
